doc: A131: the rows a mode's own rules change by design. tools/qa/accept/summarize-matrix.mjs reads this: a failing row named here is a named, by-design difference (shown as BY-DESIGN with its reason), any other failing row is UNEXPLAINED. Entries: by_design (the row cannot hold in this mode: it may pass or fail), or accept (the row holds when every check on its facts holds: {key, min?, max?}; replaces the drill's own band for this mode). Machine verdicts (exit 3) are not in this table: they are the driver's.

check.by_design: game.skater.check_enabled=false: nobody can check in the pond (no RMB hit exists)

crosscheck.by_design: game.skater.check_enabled=false: the cross-check is a hit too; the stick lift alone is not the row

checked.by_design: game.skater.check_enabled=false: nobody checks the standing human, so there is no knockdown to wait for

brake.why: top speed 16 m/s (speed 10 + breakaway 0.6): the same brake law (about 2.9 frames per m/s) stops in 46 frames; the drill's 40 is the 11 m/s game's; 52 = 3.25 frames per m/s of 16

pass.by_design: the plain cartridge is first_to 3: the drill's three shoot goals end the match after step 4, so steps 5 to 10 are never staged (the acceptance cut plays first_to 9; the 12 mode cuts and the tiers do too)
